text:
Clayton Keller is the Mammoth's playmaker in a way the box score is making very obvious: 20 assists, 5 goals, and 16 of his 25 points on the power play. Utah has leaned on him harder lately, too. He's averaged 20 minutes over his last ten games, more than two minutes above his season pace, and he logged over 22 in three of the last five.

The goals should come. He's shooting 9.4% against a talent range of about 12%, and his 6.2 expected goals say he's getting to the right places. The concern is five on five. Utah is about even in expected goals with him on the ice, but its share is 8.5 points worse than when he sits, which is a strange number for a player Evolving-Hockey rated sixth among all forwards last season. That same rating came with a warning: his results ran well ahead of his chances.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. The passing is real. What we'd watch is whether his even-strength line starts tilting the ice again, because a power-play-heavy season is harder to sustain than it looks.
headline: Keller is passing, and waiting on the goals
